A

Adam Kadmon

The cosmic structure that once unified imagination, matter, and meaning into a single coherent reality. Its collapse shattered the world into hex-shaped fragments and began the era in which the game takes place.

Advancement

The process through which characters, factions, or territory grow stronger over time through experience, development, and achievements.

Ancestry

A character’s biological origin or species, determining their innate traits and physical heritage.

Archetype

A character’s primary role or style of action within the faction. Archetypes influence available abilities and narrative identity.

B

Beat

A narrative moment where players must make a meaningful choice that affects the campaign world.

Campaign Beats drive the story forward and often introduce problems, opportunities, or revelations.

Boss

A powerful adversary represented through special raid mechanics and staged damage progression.

C

Campaign

The ongoing story created through player decisions, faction development, and narrative events.

Campaign Beat

A structured narrative encounter that presents a situation, asks for player decisions, and produces consequences that shape the world.

Character

A player-controlled individual who acts within the world and represents the faction’s interests during exploration and story events.

Crew Type

A cultural or occupational background that influences a character’s skills and worldview.

D

Darkness

A metaphysical force representing corruption, entropy, and destructive imbalance in the world.

Darkness grows when suffering, atrocity, or collapse spreads through reality.

Development

The improvement of a hex through construction, infrastructure, or social investment.

Higher development increases a faction’s stability and resource production.

E

Enlightenment

A measure of spiritual or philosophical awakening achieved by a character through experience and reflection.

Encounter

A structured situation requiring player action. Encounters may involve exploration, negotiation, puzzles, or conflict.

F

Faction

The organization controlled by the players. A faction manages territory, resources, strategic actions, and long-term goals.

Faction Tracks

Metrics representing the health and condition of a faction.

Common examples include:

• Morale
• Loyalty
• Unity
• Darkness
• Victory

Faction Turn

A cycle of strategic activity where factions spend resources, execute plans, and react to world events.

G

Gate (Ley Gate)

A mystical passage connecting distant hexes through the flow of magical resonance.

Ley Gates allow rapid travel across the world when activated.

GM (Game Master)

The person responsible for presenting the world, running encounters, and interpreting the rules.

Great Work

The long-term effort to restore harmony and stability to the shattered world.

Player factions contribute to the Great Work by repairing infrastructure, resolving conflicts, and confronting sources of corruption.

H

Hazard

A dangerous environmental condition encountered during exploration or travel.

Examples include radiation zones, corrupted terrain, or unstable magical fields.

Hex

A region of the map representing a fragment of the broken world.

Hexes contain:

• locations
• resources
• threats
• opportunities

Hex Development Cycle

The process through which a hex evolves as players invest resources and resolve problems.

I

Integration

A measure of how strongly a hex is connected to faction infrastructure and governance.

L

Leyline

A current of magical energy flowing through the world and connecting distant regions.

Logistics

The ability of a faction to support expansion, travel, and infrastructure through supply and organization.

M

Maneuver

A tactical action used during raids to influence the outcome of a conflict.

Mal

The narrative voice of the system itself — a semi-aware perspective through which the game world occasionally speaks.

Morale

A measure of faction confidence, optimism, and emotional stability.

Low morale can lead to instability or collapse.

O

Occult Association

A character’s connection to hidden magical traditions or supernatural organizations.

Operations Points (OP)

The primary resource used by factions to perform strategic actions.

Different OP types represent different forms of influence and capability.

OP Regeneration

The process by which factions regain Operations Points each turn.

P

Political Philosophy

The ideological framework guiding a character’s beliefs about governance, power, and social organization.

Political philosophies influence faction cohesion and internal tension.

Pressure

The accumulation of stress on a faction caused by conflict, resource shortages, or political instability.

R

Raid

A structured conflict system used to resolve large-scale confrontations between factions, bosses, or obstacles.

Raids use tactical maneuvers and faction resources to determine outcomes.

Resonance

A measure of how strongly magical forces respond to a character or location.

S

Scenario

A defined encounter structure used by the game engine to run complex situations such as raids or boss fights.

Sephirotic Alignment

A spiritual or metaphysical alignment representing a character’s philosophical orientation toward cosmic balance.

Strategic Activity

A major faction action performed during the faction turn.

Examples include:

• development
• construction
• raids
• diplomacy

Strain

The accumulation of magical or metaphysical stress experienced by characters using powerful abilities.

T

Territory

The collection of hexes controlled or influenced by a faction.

Turn

A structured cycle of time in which factions perform actions and the world evolves.

Travel

Movement between hexes, often involving exploration and potential encounters.

U

Unity

A measure of cohesion within a faction.

High unity indicates strong cooperation, while low unity may lead to internal conflict.

V

Victory

A measure of faction success and influence within the wider world.

Victory represents the progress of a faction toward long-term goals.

W

War Log

A record of major faction actions, conflicts, and outcomes.

World Mutation

A change to the game world resulting from player actions or narrative events.

World State

The cumulative condition of the campaign world, shaped by all past events and faction activity.

X

Xenofauna

Strange creatures emerging from corrupted or unstable regions of reality.

Z

Zone

A geographic or environmental category used to group similar hexes.
